title: Archetype
description: A specialisation chosen within a class, picked at a level the class sets and kept for the rest of a character's career. An archetype is where a class's identity actually gets decided, so it carries its own casting progression when it grants one and a level-by-level table when its resources grow on their own schedule.

key.description: Stable slug identifying this archetype. Derived from the name once and never reused, so saved characters keep resolving after a rename.

name.description: Display name. Archetype names in SW5e are noun phrases naming the discipline rather than the practitioner: Acquisitions Practice, Armormech Engineering.

className.description: Name of the class this archetype belongs to, matching a class entry. An archetype is only ever available to that one class.

casterType.description: Casting the archetype grants by itself. An archetype on a non-casting class may turn it into a partial caster; one on a class that already casts records none here and leaves the progression to the class.

casterRatio.description: Fraction of class levels that count toward the casting progression this archetype grants: 1/3 for a third-caster, 1/6 for a sixth-caster, 0 when it grants none. Multiclass casting sums these ratios, which is why it is a number and not a label.

classCasterType.description: Casting the parent class already provides, copied here so an archetype can be evaluated without loading the class. When this and casterType disagree, the archetype is adding a second casting system to the character.

description.description: Markdown body of the archetype: an opening paragraph of flavour, then each granted feature under its own heading with the level it arrives at. Individual features are also stored separately in the feature content type; this field is the printed page.

progression.description: The archetype's own level table, one row per character level from the level the archetype is taken. Present only when the archetype grants resources that grow on a schedule of their own, such as force points or superiority dice; omit it when every grant is described in the text instead. Column headings are the entry labels, which are the same on every row.

level.description: Character level this row applies at.

entries.description: Cells in the row, in printed column order.

label.description: Column heading, such as Force Points or Superiority Dice Size.

value.description: Cell contents. Text rather than a number because cells hold values like 1st and d8 alongside plain counts.

sourceKey.description: Key of the source this archetype was published in, matching a document of the source content type. Values present in the archive are phb and ec.

contentSet.description: Whether this archetype belongs to the core rules or to the community expanded-content supplement.
